audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize an exceptional fuel-margin year as durable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified actual; using the FY2024-FY2025 average fuel margin of 39.08 cents instead of 42.57 cents computes to $122.680 million pretax, and reducing RIN income from $35.410 million to FY2025's $16.664 million adds $18.746 million, for a combined $141.426 million pretax or $107.767 million after the filed 23.8% tax rate, equal to 15.6% of the $691.0 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inflates FY2026 OE and the fitted log-trend anchor, which then scales projected OE, terminal value, and every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal year, particularly in the last quarter, the Company, and the retail fuel industry, experienced historically higher than average fuel revenue less cost of goods sold per gallon (excluding depreciation and amortization).
audit_findings.explanation: The exceptional margin is demonstrated by the filing, but a specific normalized margin and resulting anchor error are not. The computed sensitivity is large relative to the anchor and is reasonably capable of materially changing the estimated valuation range, although a downward correction would not close the gap between the $394.23 bull value and the $756.09 market price.
audit_findings.action: Normalize fuel margin using an evidenced multi-year or cycle measure, normalize RIN income separately, recompute after-tax OE for affected years, refit the log trend, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The valuation may treat operating liquidity as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified actual; maximum bridge exposure is the filed $522.991 million, or $13.95 per diluted share, equal to 4.1% of the $336.81 base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any required operating cash should be excluded from the cash-and-short-term-investments amount added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the nature of our business, cash provided by operations is our primary source of liquidity.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire cash balance is demonstrated, but the filing does not establish how much cash is operationally required. Even the conservative extreme of removing all $522.991 million lowers base value by only $13.95 per share and cannot change the conclusion relative to the $756.09 market price; the actual effect must be smaller than that maximum.
audit_findings.action: Document minimum cash needed for payroll, inventory purchases, card settlement timing, and seasonality, then add only the demonstrated surplus in a bridge sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Noncash finance-lease investment may escape both capex and the equity claim bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified actual; filed FY2026 finance-lease additions were $20.980 million and principal payments were $10.416 million, versus three-year averages of $18.440 million and $9.646 million, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease amortization is added back in OE while neither noncash asset additions nor principal repayments are captured by maintenance capex, recurring asset consumption is omitted from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company records operating lease liabilities within its own financial statement caption, broken out between current and long-term, and records finance lease liabilities within current maturities of long-term debt and finance lease obligations and long-term debt and finance lease obligations on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The finance-lease additions, amortization, and principal payments are demonstrated, but the record does not show how the maintenance-capex estimate treated them. The current annual amounts are only 1.4%-3.0% of the $691.0 million anchor, but the treatment across the full OE history and the resulting trend effect cannot be established, so materiality remains unresolved rather than a demonstrated error.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a 2017-2026 finance-lease rollforward reconciling amortization added back, noncash additions, principal payments, and maintenance capex; capture the recurring economic cost exactly once, refit the anchor, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The asset-retirement obligation may be an unbridged senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum filed exposure of $54.555 million, or $1.46 per diluted share, equal to 0.43% of the $336.81 base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Tank-removal costs must enter either normalized maintenance capex or the equity bridge as a senior liability, without double counting accretion expense.
audit_findings.evidence: The discounted liability was $ 54,555 and $ 52,105 at April 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and is recorded in other long-term liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is demonstrated, but omission from OE is not because removal spending may already be represented in maintenance capex. Even deducting the entire filed liability from the bridge would reduce value by only $1.46 per share and would not affect the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile historical tank-removal cash spending to maintenance capex; if it is excluded, deduct the $54.555 million ARO in the bridge while preventing double counting of accretion or included removal expenditures.

audit_findings.title: A disclosed one-time gift-card benefit remains in the latest OE observation
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.000 million pretax and $6.096 million after the filed 23.8% tax rate; 0.88% of the $691.0 million anchor, with a conservative one-for-one anchor sensitivity of $106.8 million or $2.85 per share in base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Inflates FY2026 OE and can marginally raise the fitted log-trend anchor and all scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, other revenue and other revenue less cost of goods sold (excluding depreciation and amortization) was favorably impacted by a one-time adjustment of $8,000 due to a change in estimate related to breakage assumptions on the outstanding gift card liability balance in the second fiscal quarter.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring benefit is demonstrated. Its after-tax amount is less than 1% of the anchor, and because it affects only one of ten trend observations, the fitted-anchor effect should be smaller than the stated one-for-one sensitivity. It cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $8.000 million pretax benefit and its tax effect from FY2026 OE, refit the log trend, and retain the resulting minor difference in the audit trail.
